key_idea: Every proper substring lies inside one of the two substrings of length n-1, so only those two need checking against s+s.
sketch: If reverse(t) is a cyclic substring then so is the reverse of any substring of t, hence it suffices to test the two maximal proper substrings s[0..n-2] and s[1..n-1]. Reverse each and search for it in s+s (any window of length n-1 of the doubled string lies inside one rotation). With n<=1000 a plain find is O(n^2) worst case, which is trivial. Corner case n=1: only the empty proper substring, answer 1. Stress-tested against a full brute force over all substrings on small strings.
